js.runLine: apify run                        # run locally; the only command that sets up the Apify environment and local storage
js.logCensoring: It censors tokens and credentials; output from `console.log` is not censored.
js.abortingRule: In the `aborting` handler, persist state, then `await Actor.exit()`, so a stopped run ends quickly and cheaply.
js.localToken: locally it uses the credentials stored by `apify login`.

python.runLine: apify run                        # run locally; the only command that sets up the Apify environment and local storage
python.logCensoring: It censors tokens and credentials; output from `print` and the standard `logging` module is not censored.
python.abortingRule: In the `aborting` handler, persist state, then `await Actor.exit()`, so a stopped run ends quickly and cheaply.
python.localToken: locally it uses the credentials stored by `apify login`.

rust.runLine: cargo run                        # run locally; reads storage/key_value_stores/default/INPUT.json and writes to storage/
rust.logCensoring: Unlike the JavaScript and Python SDKs, the Rust SDK does not censor tokens and credentials in the log, so never log them.
rust.abortingRule: On `aborting`, the SDK exits the Actor by itself (`Actor::init` sets that up). In an `aborting` handler only persist state; never call `Actor::exit()` inside an event handler, as `exit` waits for the handlers to finish.
rust.localToken: locally `cargo run` does not read the credentials stored by `apify login`, so set `APIFY_TOKEN` in the environment when the code needs the API.
